history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Initial check using standard equivalences: 1) and 2) are De Morgan’s laws—both valid. 3) (A → B) ↔ (¬B → ¬A) is the contrapositive equivalence and is valid. 4) (A → B) ↔ (¬A ∨ B) is the canonical implication rewrite—valid. 6) ¬(A → B) ↔ (A ∧ ¬B) is the definition of when an implication fails—valid. 5) (¬A → B) rewrites to (A ∨ B), not (A ∨ ¬B). Therefore, (¬A → B) ↔ (A ∨ ¬B) is the outlier (not equivalent).
